requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

The two marked tests are `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules]`.

- **Anchor and in-source reference contribute their selection.**
  - The first test uses a declaration with `:impl: src/lib.rs#fn[api]` plus an in-source `{impl}` reference. It asserts exactly one `src/lib.rs` input with item `fn[api]`, so the two sources are deduplicated.
  - That input's text contains `helper();` but not `fn helper`. This shows helpers are not supplied recursively.
- **An in-source reference alone selects its enclosing node.** The test drops the anchor and asserts the mandatory inputs are identical to the anchored case.
- **A file with no outline selects the whole file.** The test adds `src/details.txt`, a plain-text file with an `{impl}` reference. It asserts an input with `item == ""` and the full file text.
- **Refining declarations contribute their complete text.** The test asserts an input for `requirements.refined` that contains both paragraphs.
- **An implementation anchor alone is enough.** The test uses `pub fn api() {}` with no in-source reference and asserts the structural mode is selected.
- **Exclusions, errors and generated evidence.** The second test covers these cases.
  - An explicit disallow aborts with an error containing "disallowed".
  - A missing node (`fn[missing]`) is reported as an error.
  - Generated `evidence/` output is omitted by default and included under an explicit allow.
  - An omitted generated `:test:` edge does not override a real implementation, and an allowed one does.
- **Non-structural cases.** The first test asserts that examples, distributed requirements, and requirements with no reachable implementation roots do not select the structural mode.

**Known gap, acknowledged**

The requirement says implementation roots MUST contribute "including when the requirement also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors".

- The tests do not check that. In the first test, once a `{test}` reference is added, it asserts `!tested.structural` and that no `fn[api]` input is present.
- Another assertion has `:test:` replace `:impl:` and expects the structural mode to be off.
- These assertions pin an "accepted compromise" in which mixed requirements omit implementation roots. That contradicts the requirement text.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_with_context]` carries a `{fixme}` on `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`. It names the same gap: mixed requirements omit roots, and the input tests "do not yet verify the full mixed-input contract".
- That fixme names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#51`, which is open, so it acknowledges this gap.

I found no other unacknowledged gaps. The remaining obligations have tests with real assertions.

selection to the initial mandatory inputs under

:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and the existing source-access
policy; omitted generated evidence MUST NOT count as an edge. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
